title: Dimer models and lozenge tilings
summary: Lattice statistical mechanics with the hexagonal dimer model as worked case: the triangular lattice, lozenge tilings as perfect matchings, height functions, combinatorial simple connectivity with a bridge from topology, flips and Thurston's criterion; Kasteleyn's theorem and determinantal local statistics on finite simply connected regions; Gibbs specifications on finite-alphabet subshifts with a proper countable-group action (tail lemma, Bernoulli ergodicity, face property, closedness) and the dimer specification on periodic graphs; slopes and the classification on the boundary of the slope triangle; torus tilings and torus limits; the four-determinant torus formula; the explicit determinantal ergodic Gibbs measure of every interior slope, identified with the incomplete beta kernel and the discrete sine kernel; local-statistics convergence of tilings of growing regions.

layers.title: The triangular lattice and lozenge tilings

targets.name: TriFace
targets.statement: The triangular lattice on ℤ×ℤ: edges (v,k), k∈{1,2,3}, from v to v+e_k with e₁=(1,0), e₂=(0,1), e₃=(1,1) (carrier TriEdge); white faces W(v)={v,v+e₁,v+e₃} and black faces B(v)={v,v+e₂,v+e₃} (carrier TriFace) with their edges; translations and the rotation ρ(x,y)=(−y,x−y).

api.name: edge_mem_two_faces
api.statement: Every edge lies in exactly two faces, one white and one black: (v,1)∈W(v),B(v−e₂); (v,2)∈B(v),W(v−e₁); (v,3)∈W(v),B(v).

api.name: faces_share_le_one_edge
api.statement: Two distinct faces share at most one edge, and faces sharing an edge have opposite colours.

api.name: faces_at_vertex
api.statement: Exactly six faces contain v: W(v),W(v−e₁),W(v−e₃),B(v),B(v−e₂),B(v−e₃).

api.name: rho_order_three
api.statement: ρ³=id, ρ preserves colours and maps direction k to k+1 mod 3; translations act freely preserving colours and directions.

tests.name: W0_B0_share
tests.statement: W(0) and B(0) share exactly the edge (0,3).

tests.name: rho_W0
tests.statement: ρ(W(0))=W(−e₁)={(−1,0),(0,0),(0,1)}; the reflection (x,y)↦(y,x) maps W(0) to B(0), reversing colours.

targets.name: hexGraph
targets.statement: hexGraph : SimpleGraph TriFace, two faces adjacent when distinct and sharing an edge.

api.name: hexGraph_adj_white
api.statement: W(v) is adjacent exactly to B(v), B(v−e₂), B(v+e₁).

api.name: hexGraph_edge_equiv
api.statement: The edges of hexGraph are in bijection with TriEdge via the shared edge.

api.name: hexGraph_bipartite_locallyFinite
api.statement: hexGraph is 3-regular, locally finite and bipartite; translations and ρ are automorphisms; faces at a vertex form a 6-cycle.

tests.name: nbrs_W0
tests.statement: Neighbours of W(0): B(0), B(−e₂), B(e₁); W(0) and B(1,−1) meet only at (1,0) and are not adjacent.

tests.name: hexagon_cycle
tests.statement: Faces at 0 form the cycle W(0)–B(0)–W(−e₁)–B(−e₃)–W(−e₃)–B(−e₂)–W(0).

tests.name: vertex_adjacency_wrong
tests.statement: Adjacency by a shared vertex would create odd cycles (W(0), W(e₁), B(1,−1) pairwise share vertices).

targets.name: TriRegion.boundaryVertices
targets.statement: For a set R of faces: V(R), E(R), interior edges E°(R) (both faces in R), boundary edges E∂(R) (exactly one face in R), boundary vertices ∂R, the boundary graph, connectedness of (V(R),E(R)), the union of faces F(R)⊆ℝ²; for a vertex set V the region Faces(V) (Aggarwal's induced-subgraph convention).

api.name: three_card_eq
api.statement: For finite R, 3|R| = 2|E°(R)| + |E∂(R)|.

api.name: not_mem_boundary_iff
api.statement: v∈V(R)∖∂R iff all six faces at v lie in R.

api.name: aggarwal_boundary_eq
api.statement: If every vertex of V lies in a face of Faces(V), Aggarwal's boundary of V equals ∂(Faces(V)).

api.name: region_equivariant
api.statement: All constructions commute with translations and ρ.

tests.name: single_face
tests.statement: R={W(0)}: no interior edge, three boundary edges, 3=2·0+3.

tests.name: unit_hexagon
tests.statement: Unit hexagon R₆: six interior edges, six boundary edges, ∂R₆ the six neighbours of 0, 18=2·6+6.

tests.name: faces_of_vertex_set
tests.statement: Faces({(0,0),(1,0)})=∅ although the induced subgraph has an edge.

targets.name: IsTiling
targets.statement: IsTiling R M: M is a set of edges each lying in two faces of R, and every face of R contains exactly one edge of M; free tilings drop the first condition and require M⊆E(R); IsPlaneTiling M for R all faces.

api.name: lozenges_partition
api.statement: The lozenges of a tiling partition R; a finite tileable R has |R|=2|M| and equally many white and black faces.

api.name: free_tiling_isTiling_iff
api.statement: A free tiling of R is a tiling iff it contains no boundary edge; restrictions of plane tilings are free tilings.

api.name: tiling_equivariant
api.statement: Translations and ρ map tilings to tilings of the image region.

tests.name: hexagon_two_tilings
tests.statement: The unit hexagon has exactly the tilings T_a={(0,3),((−1,0),1),((0,−1),2)} and T_b={(0,1),(0,2),((−1,−1),3)}.

tests.name: single_face_free
tests.statement: {W(0)} has no tiling and three free tilings.

tests.name: union_not_tiling
tests.statement: M₁∪M₃ is not a plane tiling: W(0) contains two of its edges.

targets.name: isTiling_iff_isPerfectMatching
targets.statement: For every region R, sending a tiling M to the subgraph of hexGraph.induce R whose edges are the pairs of faces sharing an edge of M is a bijection from the tilings of R onto the perfect matchings of hexGraph.induce R; for R all faces, plane tilings are the perfect matchings of hexGraph.
hypotheses: R : Set TriFace arbitrary (finite or infinite)

tests.name: empty_region
tests.statement: R=∅: one tiling, one (empty) perfect matching.

tests.name: single_face_none
tests.statement: R={W(0)}: neither side has an element.

tests.name: hexagon_C6
tests.statement: Unit hexagon: two tilings and the 6-cycle has two perfect matchings.

targets.name: rowTiling
targets.statement: Row tilings M_ε={((x,y),1):ε_x=1}∪{((x,y),3):ε_x=0} for ε∈{0,1}^ℤ (column x filled with type-1 lozenges when ε_x=1, with unit squares when ε_x=0), with the shift (σε)_x=ε_{x−1}; the frozen tilings M₁, M₂, M₃ are M_1, the all-direction-2 tiling and M_0.

api.name: rowTiling_isPlaneTiling
api.statement: M_ε is a plane tiling: W(x,y) contains ((x,y),1) or ((x,y),3) and B(x,y) contains ((x,y+1),1) or ((x,y),3) according as ε_x=1 or 0, and no other edge.

api.name: rowTiling_noType2_injective
api.statement: M_ε has no direction-2 edge, hence no type-2 lozenge; ε↦M_ε is injective with ε_x=[((x,0),1)∈M_ε] and continuous for the product topologies.

api.name: rowTiling_translate
api.statement: τ_{e₂}M_ε=M_ε and τ_{e₁}M_ε=M_{σε}; the constant sequences give M₁ and M₃.

tests.name: constant_sequences
tests.statement: ε≡1 gives M₁ and ε≡0 gives M₃; no ε gives M₂, whose edges have direction 2.

tests.name: column_indexing_fails
tests.statement: Reading ε along a column, {((x,y),1):ε_y=1}∪{((x,y),3):ε_y=0}, is not a tiling for ε=1_{{0}}: B(x,0) gets neither ((x,1),1) (ε_1=0) nor ((x,0),3) (ε_0=1).

layers.title: Height functions, simple connectivity and Thurston's criterion

targets.name: IsSimplyConnectedRegion
targets.statement: An edge cochain c : TriEdge → ℤ is closed on R if c(v,1)+c(v+e₁,2)=c(v,3) for W(v)∈R and c(v,2)+c(v+e₂,1)=c(v,3) for B(v)∈R, exact on R if c(u,k)=g(u+e_k)−g(u) on E(R) for some g : V(R)→ℤ; R is simply connected if nonempty, connected and every closed cochain is exact.

api.name: exact_closed
api.statement: Exact cochains are closed; primitives on connected regions are unique up to a constant.

api.name: simplyConnected_equivariant
api.statement: Simple connectivity is invariant under translations and ρ.

api.name: shelling
api.statement: Adding to a simply connected R a face meeting F(R) in exactly one edge with new opposite vertex, or in exactly two of its edges, preserves simple connectivity.

tests.name: single_face_sc
tests.statement: {W(0)} is simply connected with primitive g(0)=0, g(e₁)=c(0,1), g(e₃)=c(0,3).

tests.name: ring_not_sc
tests.statement: R_ring (the twelve faces other than W(0) meeting W(0)) carries the dual-path cochain with sum c(0,1)+c(e₁,2)−c(0,3)=1 round W(0): not simply connected.

tests.name: hexagon_shelling
tests.statement: The unit hexagon is simply connected by shelling W(0),B(0),W(−e₁),B(−e₃),W(−e₃),B(−e₂).

targets.name: isSimplyConnectedRegion_univ
targets.statement: Every cochain closed on the set of all faces is exact.

tests.name: neutral_not_closed
tests.statement: c₀ (0 on directions 1,2; 1 on direction 3) is not closed: 0+0≠1 on W(v).

tests.name: primitive_M1
tests.statement: The cochain of M₁ has primitive x; that of M₃ has primitive 0.

tests.name: plane_minus_face
tests.statement: On all faces except W(0) the dual-path cochain is closed and not exact.

targets.name: not_isSimplyConnectedRegion_of_hole
targets.statement: If R is nonempty and Q is a nonempty finite set of faces outside R such that every face sharing an edge with a face of Q lies in Q∪R, then R is not simply connected; for finite simply connected R the complement is connected through shared edges.
hypotheses: Q finite nonempty, disjoint from R, closed under edge-adjacency outside R

tests.name: ring_hole
tests.statement: R_ring with Q={W(0)} satisfies the hypothesis.

tests.name: fan_not_enclosed
tests.statement: The five faces at 0 other than W(0) with Q={W(0)} fail the hypothesis (B(e₁) is outside both); that region is simply connected.

tests.name: empty_region
tests.statement: R=∅: vacuous, since simple connectivity includes nonemptiness.

targets.name: IsSimplyConnected.isSimplyConnectedRegion
targets.statement: If F(R)⊆ℝ² satisfies IsSimplyConnected then IsSimplyConnectedRegion R.

tests.name: triangle
tests.statement: F({W(0)}) is a convex triangle; both notions hold.

tests.name: wedge
tests.statement: W(0) and B(1,1) meeting at (1,1): F(R) a wedge of triangles, simply connected; cochains glue at (1,1).

tests.name: ring
tests.statement: F(R_ring) is not simply connected; 2.3 shows R_ring is not either.

targets.name: planeHeight_bijective
targets.statement: For every plane tiling M there is a unique H_M : ℤ²→ℤ with H_M(0)=0, H_M(v+e₁)−H_M(v)=[(v,1)∈M], H_M(v+e₂)−H_M(v)=[(v,2)∈M], H_M(v+e₃)−H_M(v)=1−[(v,3)∈M]; M↦H_M is a bijection onto the height functions (increments in {0,1} along e₁,e₂,e₃) vanishing at 0.

api.name: planeHeight_translate
api.statement: H_{τ_w M}(v)=H_M(v−w)−H_M(−w).

api.name: planeHeight_rotate
api.statement: H_{ρM}(w)=H_M(ρ⁻¹w)+w₁.

api.name: planeHeight_lipschitz
api.statement: H_M(u+(a,b))−H_M(u) ≤ max(a,b,0).

api.name: gorin_height
api.statement: Gorin's height is x+y−3H_M.

tests.name: frozen_heights
tests.statement: H_{M₁}=x, H_{M₂}=y, H_{M₃}=0; for the row tiling H_{M_ε}(x,y)=Σ_{0≤i<x}ε_i for x≥0 and −Σ_{x≤i<0}ε_i for x<0 (for ε≡1 and x=−1 this is −1, not the empty sum 0); for alternating ε_x=[x odd] it is ⌊x/2⌋.

tests.name: floor_height
tests.statement: ⌊(x+y)/2⌋ is a height function whose tiling has no type-3 lozenge.

tests.name: x_plus_y
tests.statement: x+y is not a height function (increment 2 along e₃).

targets.name: freeTiling_equiv_height
targets.statement: For simply connected R, v₀∈V(R), m∈ℤ: free tilings of R correspond bijectively to height functions on R with H(v₀)=m, and tilings to those with neutral increments along all boundary edges.

tests.name: triangle_heights
tests.statement: {W(0)}: free tilings {(0,1)},{(e₁,2)},{(0,3)} give (H(e₁),H(e₃))=(1,1),(0,1),(0,0); none is a tiling.

tests.name: ring_no_height
tests.statement: R_ring's tiling T has increments summing to −1 round W(0): no height function.

targets.name: boundaryHeight_eq
targets.statement: A finite simply connected region has connected boundary graph; if the boundary graph of R is connected and M, M' are tilings of R whose height cochains are exact on R (every tiling when R is simply connected, by 2.6), their height functions agree on ∂R after normalisation at a common boundary vertex, so the boundary height h_R depends only on R.
hypotheses: R finite and IsSimplyConnectedRegion R (first part)
boundary graph connected and the two tilings have exact height cochains on R, e.g. R simply connected (second part)

tests.name: hexagon_boundary
tests.statement: Unit hexagon: h=0 at (1,0),(1,1),(0,1), h=−1 at (−1,0),(−1,−1),(0,−1), induced by both tilings.

tests.name: strip
tests.statement: The strip between y=0 and y=1 is simply connected with two boundary components; M₃ and M₂ restricted give heights 0 and 1 on y=1.

tests.name: pinch
tests.statement: W(0) and B(1,1) at a vertex: connected boundary, no boundary height, untileable.

tests.name: pinched_ring
tests.statement: R_ring minus W(−e₃), B(−e₃): connected boundary graph (inner triangle joined to the outer boundary at 0 by ((−1,0),1)), unique tiling T∖{((−1,−1),3)} whose cochain sums to −1 round W(0): no height function, so exactness cannot be dropped.

targets.name: flip_connected
targets.statement: Minima and maxima of height functions are height functions; for finite simply connected tileable R the height functions with boundary values h_R have least and greatest elements given by ρ_R; a tiling with H≠H_min admits a downward flip staying ≥H_min; any two tilings are joined by finitely many flips; all tilings have the same numbers of lozenges of each type.

tests.name: hexagon_flip
tests.statement: T_a = H_max flips at 0 to T_b = H_min; H_max(0)−H_min(0)=1.

tests.name: three_cycle
tests.statement: The flip changes W(0)–B(0), W(−e₁)–B(−e₃), W(−e₃)–B(−e₂) to W(0)–B(−e₂), W(−e₁)–B(0), W(−e₃)–B(−e₃).

tests.name: torus_frozen
tests.statement: On the 2×2 torus the two tilings of height change (1,0) admit no flip.

targets.name: thurston_tileable_iff
targets.statement: For finite connected R: a boundary function h : ∂R→ℤ with neutral increments along boundary edges and h(v)−h(u)≤ρ_R(u,v) exists iff R has a tiling with exact height cochain, given by H=min_u(h(u)+ρ_R(u,·)); for simply connected R, R is tileable iff such h exists.
hypotheses: IsSimplyConnectedRegion R for the tileability form

tests.name: hexagon_ok
tests.statement: Unit hexagon: h exists and the inequalities hold.

tests.name: triangle_no_h
tests.statement: {W(0)}: c₀ sums to −1 round the triangle; no h.

targets.name: card_direction_diff_eq
targets.statement: If plane tilings M, M' differ on finitely many edges, then for each k, M∖M' and M'∖M contain equally many edges of direction k.

tests.name: hexagon_counts
tests.statement: T_a∖T_b and T_b∖T_a each contain one edge of each direction.

tests.name: frozen_infinite
tests.statement: M₁ and M₃ differ on infinitely many edges with densities 1 and 0.

tests.name: row_column
tests.statement: M_ε and M_ε' with ε,ε' differing at one site differ along a whole column.

layers.title: Kasteleyn theory on finite simply connected regions

targets.name: kasteleynMatrix
targets.statement: For finite R and a positive edge weight w: K_R (rows white faces, columns black faces, entry w(e) for faces sharing e, else 0), partitionFunction R w = Σ_{M∈𝔈(R)} ∏_{e∈M} w(e), and, when the partition function is positive (for positive w, exactly when R is tileable), the Boltzmann probability measure on 𝔈(R) with masses proportional to the weights; the matrix and the partition function are defined for every finite R.

api.name: kasteleyn_square_iff
api.statement: K_R is square iff R has equally many white and black faces; otherwise 𝔈(R)=∅.

api.name: kasteleyn_det_bijection
api.statement: Determinants for two bijections differ by a sign; the inverse (rows black, columns white) is independent of the bijection.

api.name: kasteleyn_entries
api.statement: At most three nonzero entries per row and column; equivariance under translations and ρ.

tests.name: hexagon_matrix
tests.statement: Unit hexagon: [[1,0,1],[1,1,0],[0,1,1]], det 2; swapping two columns gives −2.

tests.name: hexagon_weighted
tests.statement: Type weights (a,b,c): [[c,0,a],[b,a,0],[0,c,b]], det 2abc = abc + abc.

tests.name: single_face
tests.statement: {W(0)}: one row, no column, partition function 0, and no Boltzmann probability measure (𝔈(R)=∅); the empty region has the empty tiling, partition function 1 and the point-mass Boltzmann measure.

targets.name: partitionFunction_eq_abs_det
targets.statement: For finite simply connected R with equally many white and black faces and positive w, all nonzero Leibniz terms of the square Kasteleyn matrix have the same sign; |det| = partitionFunction R w, and = #𝔈(R) for w≡1.

tests.name: hexagon
tests.statement: Unit hexagon: 2, and 2abc with type weights.

tests.name: ring_fails
tests.statement: R_ring: dual 12-cycle, two tilings differing by an odd 6-cycle; det 0 while the partition function is 2.

targets.name: sum_perm_fixing_eq_det_mul_det_inv
targets.statement: For invertible square A over a field with rows I and columns J identified by a bijection, distinct rows i_l and columns j_l: Σ_{σ(i_l)=j_l} sgn(σ)∏_{i∉{i_l}} A(i,σi) = det A · det[(A⁻¹)(j_l,i_m)].

tests.name: k_one
tests.statement: k=1: Mathlib's adjugate entry det A·(A⁻¹)(j,i).

tests.name: repeated_row
tests.statement: i₁=i₂: empty sum versus two equal columns; both 0.

targets.name: lozenge_correlation_eq_det
targets.statement: For finite simply connected R with positive partition function, positive w and pairwise distinct pairs (f_i,g_i) of white and black faces: the Boltzmann probability that each f_i is matched to g_i is ∏K(f_i,g_i)·det[K⁻¹(g_i,f_j)].

tests.name: hexagon_one
tests.statement: Unit hexagon: P(W(0)–B(0)) = K⁻¹(B(0),W(0)) = 1/2.

tests.name: shared_face
tests.statement: Pairs sharing B(0): equal rows, probability 0.

targets.name: tailSigma
targets.statement: For a countable infinite group Γ acting properly on a countable set I (for finite F,F' only finitely many γ have γF∩F'≠∅) and Ω = I → S with the product σ-algebra: the outside σ-algebras 𝓕_{Λᶜ}, the tail σ-algebra 𝓣 = ⋂_{Λ finite} 𝓕_{Λᶜ}, cylinder events, and the action (γω)(i)=ω(γ⁻¹i).

api.name: tail_invariant
api.statement: 𝓣 is a sub-σ-algebra invariant under the action; tail events are unchanged by finitely many coordinate changes.

api.name: cylinder_ring
api.statement: Cylinder events form a ring of sets generating the product σ-algebra.

api.name: tail_eq_tailProcess
api.statement: For I infinite (forced by properness unless I=∅) and any enumeration e:ℕ≃I, 𝓣 = TauCeti.Probability.tailProcess (fun k ω => ω (e k)), by tailProcess_eq_iInf_tailFamily and cofinality of the sets e([0,n)) among finite Λ; this is the limsup-atTop form Mathlib's measure_zero_or_one_of_measurableSet_limsup_atTop consumes, independent of e.

tests.name: infinitely_many_ones
tests.statement: On {0,1}^ℤ the event 'infinitely many ones' lies in 𝓣 and in tailProcess along any enumeration of ℤ; 'ω(0)=1' lies in neither.

tests.name: finite_index
tests.statement: For finite I the tail σ-algebra is trivial.

tests.name: non_proper
tests.statement: ℤ acting trivially on a point is not proper; the invariant event ω(pt)=1 has measure 1/2 under (δ₀+δ₁)/2 and is not a.s. tail.

targets.name: exists_tail_ae_eq_of_invariant
targets.statement: If μ is a Γ-invariant probability measure on Ω and A is measurable with γA=A for all γ, some tail event T has μ(AΔT)=0.
hypotheses: Γ countable infinite, proper action on countable I

locator.where: Lemma 3.2.2, lines 1367–1371 (ingredient of its proof; georgii2011 Theorem 14.15)

tests.name: density_event
tests.statement: The shift-invariant event 'the density of ones is 1/2' is itself tail.

tests.name: finite_group
tests.statement: For the trivial group on a point the conclusion fails as in 4.1.

tests.name: point_mass
tests.statement: Under the point mass at a constant configuration take T∈{∅,Ω}.

targets.name: ergodicSMul_infinitePi
targets.statement: For a probability measure ν on S, ν^{⊗I} (Measure.infinitePi) is Γ-invariant, trivial on 𝓣 and ErgodicSMul Γ Ω ν^{⊗I}.

tests.name: bernoulli_shift
tests.statement: The two-sided Bernoulli(1/2) shift on {0,1}^ℤ is ergodic.

tests.name: dirac
tests.statement: ν=δ_a gives the point mass at a constant configuration, ergodic.

tests.name: mixture
tests.statement: (Bern(1/3)^{⊗ℤ}+Bern(2/3)^{⊗ℤ})/2 is invariant and not ergodic.

targets.name: tendsto_iff_cylinder_tendsto
targets.statement: For finite S and closed Γ-invariant X⊆Ω: X is compact metrisable, cylinder events are clopen, ProbabilityMeasure X is compact, Γ acts by affine homeomorphisms, μ_n→μ iff μ_n(C)→μ(C) for all cylinder events C; for S=Bool correlation functions determine μ and their convergence is weak convergence.

tests.name: receding_indicator
tests.statement: Point masses at 1_{[n,∞)} converge to the point mass at 0.

tests.name: one_point_insufficient
tests.statement: Bern(1/2)^{⊗ℤ} and (δ_0+δ_1)/2 share the one-point function 1/2 but have two-point functions 1/4 and 1/2.

tests.name: not_closed
tests.statement: Finitely supported configurations are not closed: point masses at 1_{[0,n]} converge to that at 1_{[0,∞)}.

targets.name: Specification
targets.statement: A specification on X: Markov kernels γ_Λ (Λ⊆I finite) from X to X, measurable for the trace of 𝓕_{Λᶜ} on X, proper (γ_Λ(B∩C|ω)=1_B(ω)γ_Λ(C|ω) for B∈𝓕_{Λᶜ}) and consistent (γ_Δγ_Λ=γ_Δ for Λ⊆Δ); μ is Gibbs if μγ_Λ=μ for all Λ; Γ-equivariance and quasilocality.

api.name: isGibbs_iff_condExp
api.statement: μ is Gibbs iff γ_Λ(C|·) is a version of the conditional expectation of 1_C given 𝓕_{Λᶜ}.

api.name: gibbs_convex
api.statement: The Gibbs measures form a convex set.

api.name: gibbs_equivariant
api.statement: For Γ-equivariant γ the Gibbs measures form a Γ-invariant set; 𝒢_inv and 𝔓_inv denote invariant elements.

tests.name: identity_spec_constants
tests.statement: On the closed shift-invariant subshift X₀={0̄,1̄} of constant configurations of {0,1}^ℤ, each trace of 𝓕_{Λᶜ} is the full σ-algebra, so γ_Λ(·|ω)=δ_ω is a specification and every probability measure on X₀ is Gibbs.

tests.name: identity_full_product
tests.statement: The identity kernels on all of {0,1}^ℤ are not a specification: for Λ={0} and C={ω(0)=1}, configurations differing only at 0 have the same exterior but kernel values 0 and 1; under Bern(1/2)^{⊗ℤ} the conditional expectation of 1_C given 𝓕_{Λᶜ} is 1/2.

tests.name: independent_spec
tests.statement: γ_Λ = ν^{⊗Λ}⊗δ_{ω|Λᶜ}: the only Gibbs measure is ν^{⊗I}.

tests.name: inconsistent
tests.statement: Independent kernels with different laws on {i} and {i,j} violate consistency; no measure is Gibbs for both.

targets.name: gibbsInvariant_extreme_iff_ergodic
targets.statement: (a) Gibbs measures are stable under tail-measurable probability densities; (b) for Γ-equivariant γ, 𝒢_inv is a face of 𝔓_inv, so μ∈𝒢_inv is extreme in 𝒢_inv iff extreme in 𝔓_inv iff ErgodicSMul, and conditioning on invariant events of positive measure stays in 𝒢_inv; (c) for quasilocal γ, 𝒢, 𝔓_inv and 𝒢_inv are weakly closed and compact.
hypotheses: γ quasilocal and S finite for (c)

tests.name: identity_face_constants
tests.statement: Identity specification on X₀={0̄,1̄} with the shift: 𝒢_inv=𝔓_inv is the segment from δ_{0̄} to δ_{1̄}; its endpoints are the ergodic elements and the midpoint gives the invariant event {1̄} mass 1/2.

tests.name: independent_face
tests.statement: Independent specification: 𝒢_inv={ν^{⊗ℤ}}, a one-point face, ergodic by 4.3.

tests.name: non_tail_density
tests.statement: Density 2·1_{ω(0)=1} against Bern(1/2)^{⊗ℤ} is not tail-measurable and the result is not Gibbs for the independent specification.

targets.name: dimerConfigurations
targets.statement: For a locally finite simple graph G on a countable type with a proper action (on edges) of a countable infinite group Γ by automorphisms: 𝔛(G) = {ω : G.edgeSet → Bool : every vertex lies in exactly one edge e with ω e = true}.
hypotheses: G locally finite, countable vertex type

api.name: dimer_closed
api.statement: 𝔛(G) is closed, compact, metrisable and Γ-invariant; Γ acts by homeomorphisms.

api.name: dimer_perfectMatching
api.statement: 𝔛(G) is in bijection with Mathlib's perfect matchings of G.

api.name: completion_finite
api.statement: Completion sets Ω_F(ω)={ω'∈𝔛(G): ω'=ω off F} are finite and contain ω; the set of restrictions {ω'|_F : ω'∈Ω_F(ω)} is the set of η:F→Bool covering every endpoint of F exactly once together with the true edges of ω outside F, so it depends only on ω on the edges outside F sharing a vertex with F, and Ω_F(ω) is obtained by gluing these restrictions to ω|_{Fᶜ}.

tests.name: path_graph
tests.statement: ℤ with nearest-neighbour edges: exactly two configurations; for F=∅ both restriction sets are {∅} while the completion sets are the two different singletons.

tests.name: infinite_degree
tests.statement: Without local finiteness (graph statement, no group action): on vertices c,d,x_n,y_n with edges c x_n, d y_n, x_n y_n, the perfect matchings M_k={c x_k, d y_k}∪{x_n y_n : n≠k} converge to {x_n y_n : n≥1}, which leaves c and d uncovered, so closedness fails.

tests.name: C6
tests.statement: The 6-cycle: two configurations, matching 1.5.

targets.name: dimerSpecification
targets.statement: γ^w_F(·|ω) is the probability measure on Ω_F(ω) with masses ∝ ∏_{e∈ω'∩F} w(e).

api.name: dimerSpecification_spec
api.statement: γ^w is a proper consistent quasilocal specification on 𝔛(G), Γ-equivariant for Γ-invariant w, uniform for w≡1; quasilocality: for a cylinder event C on finite E, γ^w_F(C|ω) depends only on ω on E∖F and on the edges outside F sharing a vertex with F (restriction sets of 5.1).

api.name: isGibbs_iff_cylinder
api.statement: μ is Gibbs iff w(ω'∩F)·μ[ω]_E = w(ω∩F)·μ[ω']_E for finite F, ω,ω' agreeing off F, and finite E containing F and its adjacent edges.

api.name: vertex_form
api.statement: Gorin's vertex-set formulation of the Gibbs property is equivalent.

api.name: gauge_invariance
api.statement: Vertex gauge transformations of w leave γ^w unchanged.

tests.name: path_all_gibbs
tests.statement: On ℤ every completion set is a singleton and every measure is Gibbs.

tests.name: C6_boltzmann
tests.statement: On C₆ with F all edges the only Gibbs measure is the Boltzmann measure; with unit weights it gives each matching mass 1/2 (alternating weights 2 and 1 give masses 8/9 and 1/9).

tests.name: gauge
tests.statement: A gauge multiplies both matchings of C₆ by ∏g(v); weights are not determined by the specification.

targets.name: dimer_gibbsInvariant_face
targets.statement: For Γ-invariant w: 𝒢, 𝔓_inv, 𝒢_inv of γ^w are weakly closed convex and compact; 𝒢_inv is a face of 𝔓_inv; μ∈𝒢_inv is ergodic iff extreme in 𝒢_inv iff extreme in 𝔓_inv iff invariant events are trivial; conditioning on invariant events of positive measure stays in 𝒢_inv.

tests.name: path_segment
tests.statement: On ℤ with Γ=2ℤ: 𝒢_inv is the segment [δ_even, δ_odd]; the midpoint is not ergodic.

tests.name: gorin_kenyon_agree
tests.statement: Gorin's extreme-point and Kenyon's trivial-invariant-event definitions of ergodic agree.

tests.name: non_invariant_gibbs
tests.statement: On ℤ with Γ=ℤ, δ_even is Gibbs and not invariant.

targets.name: IsLozengeGibbs
targets.statement: The lozenge instance: 𝔈(𝕋) ≅ 𝔛(hexGraph) with TriEdge as edge set, ℤ² acting by τ; 𝔓(𝕋) = ProbabilityMeasure 𝔛(hexGraph); IsLozengeGibbs μ means Gibbs for the uniform specification; type weights give the uniform specification.

api.name: lozenge_proper
api.statement: hexGraph is locally finite and countable; ℤ² acts freely, colour-preservingly, properly on edges.

api.name: typeWeights_eq_uniform
api.statement: For type weights (w₁,w₂,w₃), γ^w = γ^unif.

api.name: lozenge_shift
api.statement: The action on 𝔛(hexGraph) is τ.

tests.name: frozen_gibbs
tests.statement: δ_{M₁}, δ_{M₂}, δ_{M₃} are invariant and Gibbs.

tests.name: nu3
tests.statement: (δ_{M₁}+δ_{M₂}+δ_{M₃})/3 is in 𝒢_inv and not ergodic.

tests.name: hexagon_weights
tests.statement: With type weights both hexagon tilings weigh abc, so weighted and uniform laws agree.

layers.title: Slopes and the boundary of the slope triangle

targets.name: slope
targets.statement: For μ∈𝔓_inv(𝕋): slope μ = (μ{(0,1)∈M}, μ{(0,2)∈M}).

api.name: slope_densities
api.statement: Faces lie in lozenges of types 1,2,3 with probabilities s,t,1−s−t; slope ∈ 𝒯̄.

api.name: expected_height
api.statement: E_μ[H_M(x,y)] = sx+ty.

api.name: slope_affine_continuous
api.statement: slope is affine and weakly continuous; slope(ρ_*μ)=(1−s−t,s); fibres in 𝒢_inv are compact convex.

tests.name: nu3_slope
tests.statement: ν₃ has slope (1/3,1/3).

tests.name: bernoulli_row
tests.statement: Bernoulli(s) rows: slope (s,0); W(0) in a type-3 lozenge with probability 1−s.

targets.name: slope_eq_corner_iff
targets.statement: For μ∈𝔓_inv(𝕋): slope (1,0) iff μ=δ_{M₁}; (0,1) iff δ_{M₂}; (0,0) iff δ_{M₃}; these are ergodic Gibbs measures.

tests.name: mixture_not_corner
tests.statement: (δ_{M₁}+δ_{M₂})/2 has slope (1/2,1/2).

tests.name: non_invariant
tests.statement: δ_{M_ε}, ε=1_{[0,∞)}, has μ{(0,1)∈M}=1 but is not δ_{M₁}.

tests.name: corner_face
tests.statement: Corner fibres are points, hence faces.

targets.name: slopeEdge_ergodicGibbs_equiv
targets.statement: Φ₂ (no type-2 lozenge) ≅ {0,1}^ℤ via ε(M)_x=[((x,0),1)∈M], intertwining τ_{e₁} with the shift and τ_{e₂} with id; completion sets of M∈Φ₂ are singletons; measures on Φ₂ are Gibbs; invariant μ has slope (s,0) iff μ(Φ₂)=1 and density s; μ↦ε_*μ is an affine homeomorphism onto shift-invariant measures of density s preserving ergodicity; for 0<s<1 Bern(s)^{⊗ℤ} and the block measure β_s give two distinct EGMs of slope (s,0); likewise on the other edges by ρ.

tests.name: two_point
tests.statement: P(ε₀=ε₁=1): s² versus (s+s²)/2; at s=1/2, 1/4 versus 3/8.

tests.name: corner_case
tests.statement: At s=1 the invariant probability measures concentrated on Φ₂ with slope (1,0) form {δ_{M₁}} ((δ_{M₁}+δ_{M₃})/2 has slope (1/2,0)); the only shift-invariant measure of density 1 is the point mass at the all-ones sequence.

tests.name: step_gibbs
tests.statement: δ_{M_ε} for ε=1_{[0,∞)} is Gibbs and not invariant.

targets.name: extreme_fibre_not_ergodic
targets.statement: ν₃=(δ_{M₁}+δ_{M₂}+δ_{M₃})/3 is an extreme point of the slope fibre over (1/3,1/3) in 𝒢_inv and is not ergodic; so slope fibres are not faces and Krein–Milman on a fibre does not produce ergodic measures.

tests.name: nu3_in_fibre
tests.statement: ν₃∈𝒢_inv (5.4) with slope (1/3,1/3); the invariant event M=M₁ has measure 1/3.

tests.name: corner_fibre_point
tests.statement: At a corner the fibre is a point (6.2), hence a face: the phenomenon is specific to non-corner slopes.

tests.name: alternating_row_average
tests.statement: On t=0, the average of the point masses at M_ε and M_{σε} for the alternating ε is invariant, Gibbs by 6.3(c), of slope (1/2,0) and ergodic by 6.3(e).

targets.name: heightChange
targets.statement: For n₁,n₂≥1, torus tilings are the (n₁ℤ×n₂ℤ)-invariant plane tilings; their height change (h₁,h₂) is H_M(v+(n₁,0))−H_M(v) and H_M(v+(0,n₂))−H_M(v).

api.name: heightChange_count
api.statement: h₁ (h₂) counts type-1 (type-2) lozenges on a horizontal (vertical) period segment.

api.name: type_counts
api.statement: Per fundamental domain: n₂h₁ type-1, n₁h₂ type-2 and n₁n₂−n₂h₁−n₁h₂ type-3 lozenges.

api.name: attainable
api.statement: The attainable height changes are the (a,b)∈ℕ² with n₂a+n₁b≤n₁n₂, realised by ⌊(n₂ax+n₁by)/(n₁n₂)⌋.

tests.name: one_by_one
tests.statement: n₁=n₂=1: three torus tilings with height changes (1,0),(0,1),(0,0).

tests.name: not_attained
tests.statement: (2,1) on the 2×2 torus violates 2a+2b≤4.

targets.name: torusMeasure
targets.statement: μ^{(a,b)}_{n₁,n₂} uniform on torus tilings with height change (a,b); μ^{s,t}_n = μ^{(⌊ns⌋,⌊nt⌋)}_{n,n} for (s,t)∈𝒯̄; μ^w_{n₁,n₂} Boltzmann for type weights on all torus tilings; all in 𝔓(𝕋).

api.name: torusMeasure_invariant
api.statement: Each torus measure is ℤ²-invariant.

api.name: torusMeasure_slope
api.statement: slope μ^{(a,b)}_{n₁,n₂} = (a/n₁, b/n₂).

api.name: floor_le
api.statement: ⌊ns⌋+⌊nt⌋ ≤ n for (s,t)∈𝒯̄.

tests.name: half_zero
tests.statement: n=2, (1/2,0): two row tilings of period two, each of mass 1/2, slope (1/2,0).

tests.name: two_by_two_uniform
tests.statement: μ^w_{2,2} with unit weights is uniform on nine tilings with slope (1/3,1/3).

targets.name: torusLimit_mem_gibbsInvariant_slope
targets.statement: Every weak limit point of (μ^{s,t}_n) lies in 𝒢_inv with slope (s,t); every weak limit point of μ^w_{n₁(k),n₂(k)} with n₁,n₂→∞ lies in 𝒢_inv; hence each slope fibre of 𝒢_inv over 𝒯̄ is nonempty, compact and convex.

tests.name: corner
tests.statement: (0,0): every μ^{0,0}_n is δ_{M₃}.

tests.name: half_zero_limit
tests.statement: (1/2,0): patterns on k sites with j ones have probability C(2m−k,m−j)/C(2m,m)→2^{−k}; the limit is the Bernoulli row measure.

tests.name: exact_third
tests.statement: n=3, (1/3,1/3): height change (1,1), slope exactly (1/3,1/3).

targets.name: twistedKasteleyn
targets.statement: Torus lozenges are L-orbits of plane edges, keeping their type; the signed weight of a torus lozenge is its weight times (−1)^a for a type-2 lozenge crossing the vertical seam (W(v)–B(v+e₁), v in the last column) and (−1)^b for a type-1 lozenge crossing the horizontal seam (W(v)–B(v−e₂), v in the first row); K_{ab}, (a,b)∈{0,1}², is indexed by [0,n₁)×[0,n₂) (rows W(v), columns B(v)), each entry the sum of the signed weights of the torus lozenges joining its two faces modulo L.

api.name: twisted_entries
api.statement: The row of W(v) receives three edge contributions w₃, ±w₁, ±w₂ (types 3, 1, 2) at columns v, v−e₂, v+e₁ modulo the period; contributions with the same column are added (n₁=1 or n₂=1), so an entry may vanish although its summands do not.

api.name: twisted_commute
api.statement: For type weights K_{ab} commutes with twisted translations.

api.name: twisted_leibniz
api.statement: Expanding every entry into its edge contributions, det K_{ab} is a signed sum of weights of torus tilings.

tests.name: one_by_one
tests.statement: n₁=n₂=1: K_{ab} = w₃+(−1)^b w₁+(−1)^a w₂, one entry adding three contributions; at type weights (1,1,2), K₁₁=0.

tests.name: two_by_two
tests.statement: 2×2, unit weights: det K₀₀=−3, det K₁₀=det K₀₁=det K₁₁=5.

tests.name: one_by_two
tests.statement: 1×2, unit weights: det K₁₀=−1, det K₀₁=5, so swapping seam conventions changes the matrices.

targets.name: twistedKasteleyn_sign
targets.statement: The term of a torus tiling of height change (h₁,h₂) in det K_{ab} has sign (−1)^{h₁h₂+(n₂+1+b)h₁+(n₁+1+a)h₂}.

tests.name: one_by_one_signs
tests.statement: 1×1: signs (−1)^b and (−1)^a for the type-1 and type-2 tilings.

tests.name: four_cycle
tests.statement: 2×2 floor tiling (1,1): a 4-cycle with one twist on each seam; sign −1 for a=b=0.

targets.name: torus_partitionFunction_eq
targets.statement: Σ_M ∏ w = (ε₀₀ det K₀₀ + ε₀₁ det K₀₁ + ε₁₀ det K₁₀ + ε₁₁ det K₁₁)/2 with ε_{ab}=−1 iff (a,b)≡(n₁,n₂) mod 2.

tests.name: one_by_one
tests.statement: 1×1: ((w₃+w₁+w₂)+(w₃−w₁+w₂)+(w₃+w₁−w₂)−(w₃−w₁−w₂))/2 = w₁+w₂+w₃.

tests.name: wrong_signs
tests.statement: ε₀₀=−1 on the 1×1 torus would give w₃−w₁−w₂.

targets.name: torus_correlation_eq
targets.statement: For pairwise distinct torus lozenges ℓ_i joining W(u_i) to B(v_i), with signed weights κ_{ab}(ℓ_i): P(all ℓ_i ∈ M) = (2Z)⁻¹ Σ ε_{ab} ∏κ_{ab}(ℓ_i)·c_{ab}, where c_{ab}=0 if two ℓ_i share a white or a black face and otherwise c_{ab} is the signed complementary minor of K_{ab} (sum over bijections σ with σ(u_i)=v_i of sgn σ ∏_{u∉{u_i}} K_{ab}(u,σu)); when det K_{ab}≠0, c_{ab}=det K_{ab}·det[K_{ab}⁻¹(v_i,u_j)] with this convention; the coefficients ε_{ab}det K_{ab}/(2Z) lie in [−1/2,1/2] and sum to 1.
hypotheses: lozenges pairwise distinct (as L-orbits of typed edges)

tests.name: one_by_one
tests.statement: 1×1, type-3 lozenge: ∏κ=w₃, c=1, formula w₃(1+1+1−1)/(2Z)=w₃/(w₁+w₂+w₃), 1/3 at unit weights; aggregated entries in place of κ would give 1.

tests.name: shared_faces
tests.statement: 1×1 torus, lozenges of types 1 and 3 (same W(0) and B(0)): c_{ab}=0 and the probability is 0; without the convention the complementary sum is 1 and the formula gives w₁w₃/(w₁+w₂+w₃).

targets.name: det_twistedKasteleyn_eq_prod
targets.statement: For type weights, characters z^{v₁}w^{v₂} with z^{n₁}=(−1)^a, w^{n₂}=(−1)^b diagonalise K_{ab} with eigenvalue w₃+w₂z+w₁w⁻¹; det K_{ab} = ∏(w₃+w₂z+w₁w⁻¹) and K_{ab}⁻¹(B(v'),W(v)) = (n₁n₂)⁻¹Σ z^{v'₁−v₁}w^{v'₂−v₂}/(w₃+w₂z+w₁w⁻¹).

tests.name: one_by_one
tests.statement: 1×1: the single eigenvalue w₃+(−1)^a w₂+(−1)^b w₁.

tests.name: three_by_three_singular
tests.statement: 3×3, uniform, a=b=0: eigenvalue 1+e^{2πi/3}+e^{−2πi/3}=0, det K₀₀=0.

layers.title: The explicit kernel and ergodic Gibbs measures of interior slopes

targets.name: inverseKernel
targets.statement: P̂_w(θ,φ)=w₃+w₂e^{iθ}+w₁e^{−iφ}; w liquid if the strict triangle inequalities hold; G_w(d)=(4π²)⁻¹∬e^{i(d₁θ+d₂φ)}/P̂_w dθdφ; K⁻¹_∞(B(v'),W(v))=G_w(v'−v).

api.name: zeros_simple
api.statement: For liquid w, P̂_w has exactly two zeros ±(θ₀,φ₀), θ₀,φ₀∉πℤ, with invertible real Jacobian; 1/P̂_w is integrable.

api.name: angles
api.statement: w₁G_w(−e₂)=θ₁/π, w₂G_w(e₁)=θ₂/π, w₃G_w(0)=θ₃/π (θ_k opposite w_k); for m≠0, w₁G_w((m,−1))=(−1)^m sin(θ₁m)/(πm), the value at m=0 being θ₁/π.

tests.name: degenerate_weights
tests.statement: w=(1,1,2): single zero (π,π) with singular Jacobian; excluded.

targets.name: riemannSum_tendsto
targets.statement: (a) For θ∉πℤ and large n, n or n+1 lies in W_θ={n: |θ−πj/n|>n^{−3/2} ∀j}; (b) for liquid w with zero (θ₀,φ₀), n₁(k)∈W_{θ₀}, n₂(k)→∞ with bounded ratios, the twisted Riemann sums converge to G_w(d) for each (a,b) and d, and det K_{ab}≠0 along the sequence.

tests.name: half_pi
tests.statement: W_{π/2} contains no even n (Gorin's n+2 version fails) and every odd n≥2.

tests.name: three_torus
tests.statement: The 3×3 uniform grid hits the zero, consistent with 3∉W_{2π/3}.

targets.name: exists_unique_determinantalGibbs
targets.statement: For liquid w there is a unique μ^w∈𝔓(𝕋) with μ^w{ℓ₁,…,ℓ_k∈M}=∏w(ℓ_i)·det[G_w(v_i−u_j)] for distinct lozenges ℓ_i=(W(u_i),B(v_i)); it is the weak limit of μ^w_{n₁(k),n₂(k)} along every sequence of 9.2(b); it lies in 𝒢_inv; slope μ^w=(θ₁/π,θ₂/π).

tests.name: uniform_pair
tests.statement: w=(1,1,1): type-1 lozenges at (0,0),(0,1) have probability 2/9−√3/(6π)≈0.130.

tests.name: single
tests.statement: One lozenge: densities θ_k/π summing to 1.

tests.name: shared_face
tests.statement: Lozenges sharing a face: probability 0.

targets.name: determinantalGibbs_mixing
targets.statement: For liquid w, μ^w(A∩τ_dB)→μ^w(A)μ^w(B) as |d|→∞; μ^w is ergodic under ℤ² and under ℤd₀ for every d₀≠0.

tests.name: covariance
tests.statement: Type-3 lozenges at 0 and d: covariance −w₃²G_w(d)G_w(−d)→0.

tests.name: frozen_mixing
tests.statement: Frozen point masses are mixing.

targets.name: exists_ergodicGibbs_of_slope
targets.statement: For every (s,t)∈𝒯̄ there is an ergodic translation-invariant Gibbs measure on 𝔈(𝕋) of slope (s,t).

tests.name: uniform
tests.statement: (1/3,1/3): w=(√3/2,√3/2,√3/2), a multiple of uniform weights.

tests.name: edge_needs_63
tests.statement: (1/2,0): w=(1,0,1) is not positive; edges use 6.3.

targets.name: incompleteBetaKernel
targets.statement: ξ(s,t)=e^{πis}sin(πt)/sin(π(1−s−t)); X(M)={v:(v,1)∈M}; K_ξ(v₁;v₂)=(2πi)⁻¹∫_{ξ̄}^{ξ}(1−z)^{y₁−y₂}z^{x₂−x₁−1}dz along ξ̄→1/2→ξ if y₁≥y₂ and ξ̄→−1→ξ if y₁<y₂.

api.name: complexSlope_bijective
api.statement: ξ:𝒯→ℍ is a bijection with inverse ξ↦(arg ξ/π, −arg(1−ξ)/π).

api.name: kernel_path_independent
api.statement: K_ξ depends only on v₂−v₁ and the side of crossing (Cauchy).

api.name: kernel_values
api.statement: K_ξ(v;v)=s; for m≠0, K_ξ((x,y);(x+m,y))=|ξ|^m sin(πsm)/(πm).

tests.name: diagonal
tests.statement: Diagonal value arg ξ/π = s; crossing (−∞,0) instead would give −(1−s).

tests.name: uniform_row
tests.statement: s=t=1/3: ξ=e^{πi/3}, |ξ|=1, the row kernel is the discrete sine kernel.

targets.name: incompleteBetaProcess_exists_unique
targets.statement: For ξ∈ℍ with slope (s,t) and w=(sin πs, sin πt, sin π(1−s−t)): entrywise w₁G_w(v_i−v_j−e₂)=(−1)^{(x_i−x_j)+(y_i−y_j)}|ξ|^{x_j−x_i}|1−ξ|^{y_i−y_j}K_ξ(v_j;v_i) with |ξ|=w₂/w₃, |1−ξ|=w₁/w₃, i.e. the matrices are conjugate by the diagonal of κ(x,y)=(−1)^{x+y}|ξ|^{−x}|1−ξ|^{y} up to transposition, so det[w₁G_w(v_i−v_j−e₂)]=det[K_ξ(v_i;v_j)]; μ_ξ=μ^w satisfies μ_ξ{v₁,…,v_m∈X(M)}=det[K_ξ(v_i;v_j)]; it is the unique such measure; it is an ergodic translation-invariant Gibbs measure of slope (s,t); along a row its type-1 correlations are det[S_s(x_i−x_j)] with S_s(0)=s and S_s(m)=sin(πsm)/(πm) for m≠0, the discrete sine kernel; a.s. every row has infinitely many type-1 lozenges, and M is a measurable function of X(M) on tilings where no two consecutive rows lack type-1 lozenges.

tests.name: uniform_pair
tests.statement: ξ=e^{πi/3}: s²−K_ξ(v₁;v₂)K_ξ(v₂;v₁)=2/9−√3/(6π), equal to 9.3; |ξ|=|1−ξ|=1 there alone, and the factor reduces to κ(x,y)=(−1)^{x+y}.

tests.name: sine_pair
tests.statement: Row, s=1/2: adjacent pair probability 1/4−1/π²≈0.149.

tests.name: not_injective
tests.statement: Heights 1_{x>0} on rows y≤0 and 1 or y on rows y≥1 give two tilings with the same X(M).

layers.title: Local statistics of tilings of growing regions

targets.name: LocalConvergence
targets.statement: For regions R_N, finite or infinite, probability measures μ_N on TriEdge→Bool concentrated on the closed set 𝔈(R_N), and vertices v_N: the local statistics converge to μ when τ_{−v_N*}μ_N→μ weakly, equivalently all cylinder probabilities converge.

api.name: localConvergence_cylinder
api.statement: Cylinder and correlation-function criteria (4.4).

api.name: localConvergence_shift
api.statement: Shifting all v_N by a fixed vector shifts the limit.

api.name: localConvergence_subseq
api.statement: Subsequential limits exist.

tests.name: constant
tests.statement: R_N all faces (infinite), μ_N=μ∈𝔓(𝕋), v_N=0: limit μ; for μ=δ_{M₃} every type-3 edge has probability 1.

tests.name: hexagons
tests.statement: R_N=R₆+v_N uniform: limit (δ_{T_a}+δ_{T_b})/2, not on 𝔈(𝕋).

tests.name: wrong_sign

targets.name: localLimit_isLozengeGibbs
